nodes.title: General Solutions of Trigonometric Equations
points: Principal solutions: Solutions θ satisfying 0 ≤ θ < 2π.
Zero Solutions (n ∈ ℤ): sinθ = 0 ⟹ θ = nπ; cosθ = 0 ⟹ θ = (2n + 1)π/2; tanθ = 0 ⟹ θ = nπ.
Non-Zero General Solutions:
1. sinθ = sinα ⟹ θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿ α.
2. cosθ = cosα ⟹ θ = 2nπ ± α.
3. tanθ = tanα ⟹ θ = nπ + α.
Squared Equations (Very Useful!): sin²θ = sin²α, cos²θ = cos²α, or tan²θ = tan²α ⟹ θ = nπ ± α.

nodes.title: Polar Coordinates & Solution of Triangles
points: Cartesian (x, y) to Polar (r, θ): r = √(x² + y²); tanθ = y/x.
Quadrant rule for polar angle θ: (1) 1st quad: θ = α; (2) 2nd quad: θ = π − α; (3) 3rd quad: θ = π + α; (4) 4th quad: θ = 2π − α, where α = tan⁻¹|y/x|.
Polar to Cartesian: x = r cosθ, y = r sinθ.
In any triangle ABC: A + B + C = π; sides opposite angles are a, b, c.

formulas.label: Cartesian conversion
formulas.expr: x = r cosθ , y = r sinθ

nodes.title: Sine Rule & Area of Triangle
points: Sine Rule: In ΔABC, a / sinA = b / sinB = c / sinC = 2R, where R is circumradius of ΔABC.
Side transformations: a = 2R sinA, b = 2R sinB, c = 2R sinC.
Angle transformations: sinA = a / 2R, sinB = b / 2R, sinC = c / 2R.
Area of triangle Δ: Δ = ½ ab sinC = ½ bc sinA = ½ ac sinB.
Area in terms of circumradius: Δ = abc / (4R).

formulas.label: Sine rule
formulas.expr: a / sinA = b / sinB = c / sinC = 2R

nodes.title: Cosine Rule & Projection Rule
points: Cosine Rule gives angles from sides:
cosA = (b² + c² − a²) / (2bc).
cosB = (c² + a² − b²) / (2ca).
cosC = (a² + b² − c²) / (2ab).
Alternative forms: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cosA; b² = c² + a² − 2ca cosB; c² = a² + b² − 2ab cosC.
Projection Rule expresses a side as sum of projections of other two sides:
a = b cosC + c cosB; b = c cosA + a cosC; c = a cosB + b cosA.

nodes.title: Half-Angle Formulas & Napier's Analogy
points: Let semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) / 2.
Half-Angle Sine: sin(A/2) = √[(s − b)(s − c) / (bc)].
Half-Angle Cosine: cos(A/2) = √[s(s − a) / (bc)].
Half-Angle Tangent: tan(A/2) = √[(s − b)(s − c) / (s(s − a))] = Δ / [s(s − a)].
Heron's Formula for Area: Δ = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)].
Napier's Analogy (Law of Tangents): tan[(B − C)/2] = [(b − c)/(b + c)] cot(A/2); tan[(C − A)/2] = [(c − a)/(c + a)] cot(B/2); tan[(A − B)/2] = [(a − b)/(a + b)] cot(C/2).

nodes.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Domains & Ranges
points: sin⁻¹x: Domain [−1, 1], Principal Range [−π/2, π/2].
cos⁻¹x: Domain [−1, 1], Principal Range [0, π].
tan⁻¹x: Domain ℝ, Principal Range (−π/2, π/2).
cot⁻¹x: Domain ℝ, Principal Range (0, π).
sec⁻¹x: Domain ℝ − (−1, 1), Principal Range [0, π] − {π/2}.
cosec⁻¹x: Domain ℝ − (−1, 1), Principal Range [−π/2, π/2] − {0}.
Self-Inversion: sin(sin⁻¹x) = x for x ∈ [−1, 1]; sin⁻¹(sinθ) = θ ONLY when θ ∈ [−π/2, π/2].

nodes.title: Properties of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
points: Negative Argument (Group 1 - Odd functions): sin⁻¹(−x) = −sin⁻¹x; tan⁻¹(−x) = −tan⁻¹x; cosec⁻¹(−x) = −cosec⁻¹x.
Negative Argument (Group 2 - π shift): cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹x; cot⁻¹(−x) = π − cot⁻¹x; sec⁻¹(−x) = π − sec⁻¹x.
Reciprocal Relations: sin⁻¹(1/x) = cosec⁻¹x; cos⁻¹(1/x) = sec⁻¹x; tan⁻¹(1/x) = cot⁻¹x (for x > 0).
Complementary Angles (Sum = π/2): sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2; tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2; sec⁻¹x + cosec⁻¹x = π/2.

nodes.title: Addition & Multiple Formulas for Inverse Trig
points: Addition of tan⁻¹: tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹[(x + y) / (1 − xy)] (valid when xy < 1).
If x > 0, y > 0 and xy > 1: tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = π + tan⁻¹[(x + y) / (1 − xy)].
Subtraction of tan⁻¹: tan⁻¹x − tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹[(x − y) / (1 + xy)] (valid when xy > −1).
Double Angle tan⁻¹ identities: 2 tan⁻¹x = tan⁻¹[2x / (1 − x²)] = sin⁻¹[2x / (1 + x²)] = cos⁻¹[(1 − x²) / (1 + x²)].

formulas.label: tan⁻¹ addition (xy > 1)
formulas.expr: tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = π + tan⁻¹[(x + y) / (1 − xy)]

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Proofs
points: Board Favourite #1: State and prove the Sine Rule: a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC = 2R.
Board Favourite #2: State and prove the Cosine Rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cosA.
Board Favourite #3: State and prove the Projection Rule: a = b cosC + c cosB.
Board Favourite #4: Prove that tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹[(x + y)/(1 − xy)] for xy < 1.
Board Favourite #5: Prove that sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2 for x ∈ [−1, 1].

nodes.title: MHT-CET Range Traps, Shortcuts & Triangle Tricks
points: Range Trap #1: sin⁻¹(sin(2π/3)) ≠ 2π/3! Since 2π/3 ∉ [−π/2, π/2], rewrite as sin⁻¹(sin(π − π/3)) = sin⁻¹(sin(π/3)) = π/3.
Range Trap #2: cos⁻¹(cos(7π/6)) ≠ 7π/6! Since 7π/6 ∉ [0, π], rewrite as cos⁻¹(cos(2π − 5π/6)) = cos⁻¹(cos(5π/6)) = 5π/6.
In Any Triangle ABC Shortcuts:
(1) tanA + tanB + tanC = tanA tanB tanC.
(2) cot(A/2) + cot(B/2) + cot(C/2) = cot(A/2) cot(B/2) cot(C/2).
(3) cos²A + cos²B + cos²C = 1 − 2 cosA cosB cosC.
Sides in AP / GP / HP: If a², b², c² are in AP ⟹ cotA, cotB, cotC are in AP.

formulas.label: tan sum-product in Δ
formulas.expr: tanA + tanB + tanC = tanA tanB tanC
